name: Question 4
problem:
$$
{x}^{′}=[\begin{aligned}3 & -1 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}]x+[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ -4\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the system of ODEs above. The equilibrium point of the system is $[1,\,2]^{T}.$ Which of the following is the system obtained by shifting the equilibrium to the origin?
worked_solution:
To shift the system's equilibrium from ${x}^{∗}$ to the origin, we define the deviation vector

$$
u=x-{x}^{∗}.
$$

In our case, we have

$$
u=x-[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2\end{aligned}]\,⇒\,x=u+[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2\end{aligned}]\,\text{and}\,{x}^{′}={u}^{′}.
$$

Substituting $x$ and ${x}^{′}$ into the given system, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{′} & =[\begin{aligned}3 & -1 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}]x+[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ -4\end{aligned}] \\ {u}^{′} & =[\begin{aligned}3 & -1 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}](u+[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2\end{aligned}])+[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ -4\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3 & -1 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}]u+[\begin{aligned}3 & -1 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ -4\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3 & -1 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}]u+[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 4\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ -4\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3 & -1 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}]u.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the shifted system is

$$
{u}^{′}=[\begin{aligned}3 & -1 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}]u.
$$

Question 4
?

x′=[3−121]x+[−1−4] Consider the system of ODEs above. The equilibrium point of the system is [1,2]T. Which of the following is the system obtained by shifting the equilibrium to the origin?

a
u′=[0−120]u
b
u′=[3−121]u+[12]
c
u′=[3001]u
d
u′=[3−121]u+[−1−4]
e
u′=[3−121]u
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

To shift the system's equilibrium from x∗ to the origin, we define the deviation vector u=x−x∗.

In our case, we have u=x−[12]⇒x=u+[12]andx′=u′.

Substituting x and x′ into the given system, we obtain x′=[3−121]x+[−1−4]u′=[3−121](u+[12])+[−1−4]=[3−121]u+[3−121][12]+[−1−4]=[3−121]u+[14]+[−1−4]=[3−121]u.

Therefore, the shifted system is u′=[3−121]u.
